title: Brown Rice with Carrots, No Added Fat

content.title: About
content.content: Brown rice with carrots, prepared without added fat, is a whole‑grain rice cooked together with grated carrots. The oil‑free preparation preserves the natural flavors and nutrients of both ingredients, resulting in a light, aromatic dish rich in fiber.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Brown rice retains the bran and germ, giving it more vitamins and minerals than white rice.
Carrots are high in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.
The lack of added fat makes the dish low‑calorie while still satisfying hunger thanks to fiber.
Rice with carrots is a traditional side in many Asian cuisines, often served as a simple main or accompaniment.
When stored properly, brown rice can stay fresh for up to 6 months.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, helps regulate blood sugar levels, and promotes satiety.

items.title: Source of magnesium and selenium
items.content: Magnesium aids muscle and nerve function, while selenium provides antioxidant protection.

items.title: Vitamin A from carrots
items.content: Beta‑carotene contributes to eye health, immune function, and skin health.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: No added oil makes the dish suitable for low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: Brown rice delivers slow‑release energy, beneficial for athletes and active individuals.

items.title: Arsenic content
items.content: Like all rice, brown rice may contain trace amounts of arsenic; rinsing before cooking reduces this.

items.title: Carrot allergy
items.content: Some people may experience allergic reactions to carrots.

items.title: Excess beta‑carotene
items.content: Very large portions of carrots can cause temporary yellowing of the skin (carotenemia).

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the rice as a side with vegetables, fish, or poultry. It works well in salads, soups, or as a base for vegetarian bowls. Add fresh herbs, a squeeze of lemon, or low‑sodium soy sauce for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep dry rice in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Cooked rice should be refrigerated and consumed within 3‑4 days. Reheat to at least 75 °C before eating.
